**Federated clients may be optimizing different local problems.** One device may contain mostly one label or user behavior, another a very different distribution. Several local steps can move their models far apart before averaging, producing client drift. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.05629) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.06127) [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.06378)

FedAvg combines updates, often weighted by client sample count. FedProx adds a penalty for moving away from the current global weights, limiting how far local optimization departs. SCAFFOLD uses control variates to correct systematic differences between local and global update directions.

**Stronger correction can also limit useful personalization.** Tune local steps, learning rate, participation rate, and proximal strength under realistic heterogeneous data and unreliable devices. Compare communication rounds and local compute as well as global accuracy.

Inspect worst-client and subgroup performance: an average can improve while a small group deteriorates. Secure aggregation and differential privacy address information exposure, not statistical heterogeneity. Likewise, solving drift does not establish privacy. Treat optimization, participation, fairness, and privacy as interacting but distinct design questions.

**Technical details and references.**

FedAvg averages client updates, usually weighted by participating clients' sample counts. With non-IID data, several local steps move each client toward its own objective and can produce client drift. FedProx adds $\frac\mu2\|w-w_t\|^2$ to each client's objective, discouraging excessive departure from the current global model. SCAFFOLD uses client/server control variates to correct update directions. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.05629) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.06127) [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.06378)

Tune local steps, learning rate, participation, and proximal strength under realistic heterogeneity and stragglers. Compare global accuracy with worst-client and subgroup performance, communication rounds, and compute. Averaging is not automatically privacy-preserving: gradients can leak information. Secure aggregation and properly accounted differential privacy address distinct threats, and neither eliminates statistical heterogeneity or guarantees every client benefits equally.
